title: Removing one grain never unmakes a heap, yet one grain is no heap
body: The sorites paradox, from the Greek word for heap and attributed to Eubulides of Miletus, starts from two claims that seem obviously true: a million grains of sand is a heap, and a heap minus one grain is still a heap. Apply the second claim again and again and you must call a single grain a heap, which is absurd. The culprit is **vagueness**: words like heap, bald and tall have no sharp edge. Philosophers have answered by drawing an arbitrary line, by insisting a line exists but cannot be known, or by letting truth come in degrees, and none of the fixes is painless.

slides.heading: The argument
items: 1,000,000 grains of sand is a heap
A heap minus one grain is still a heap
So 999,999 grains is a heap. And 999,998. And so on…
Eventually one grain is a heap, which is plainly false

slides.heading: A million grains is a heap. One grain is not. Where is the line?
slides.note: Every step down is one grain, and no single grain seems to make the difference.

slides.heading: Ways out
items: Draw a line: 10,000 grains is a heap, 9,999 isn’t (but why there?)
Epistemicism: there is a line, we just can’t know where it is
Fuzzy logic: being a heap comes in degrees
Deny that heaps exist at all

slides.heading: Bald men and tall people
slides.text: Swap grains for hairs and you get the falakros, from the Greek for bald: losing one hair never makes a man bald, so no one ever goes bald. Any word with blurry edges can play the game, which is why the puzzle still bothers logicians more than two thousand years on.

slides.question: What is the root of the sorites, or heap, paradox?
options: Vague words with no sharp edge
slides.explanation: Heap, bald and tall have no exact boundary, so no single grain or hair can be the one that makes the difference, yet the difference clearly appears somewhere.

slides.clue: The culprit behind the heap paradox: words like heap, bald and tall have no sharp edge
slides.detail: Philosophers answer with sharp lines, unknowable lines or degrees of truth, and none of the fixes is painless.
